text:
alex: heads-up from running the java sampleapp integration tests: on retries the span attribute 'request_id' becomes <redacted> even though logs keep the original id for the first attempt
meera: curious, is this the same symptom as the node issue we saw last month?
alex: similar but different ordering. java sample registers filters like: 
alex: ```java
server.addFilter(new OtelContextFilter()); // sets span attrs from headers
server.addFilter(new RedactFilter());     // scrubs headers for wire
server.addFilter(new RetryFilter());      // triggers retry and replay
```
alex: sequence on a retry: first attempt -> Otel grabs header and sets span attr; RetryFilter creates a new HttpRequest (copies headers) and Replay; RedactFilter then scrubs the headers on the replayed request -> but the exporter picks up span attr from the (copied) context which now has the redacted header value
ryan: hmm that ordering makes it easy to hit: exporter reads attribute from context at export time, and redaction mutated the copy used by the replay.
meera: Java behavior differs from python cause python retry returns a fresh context that preserves the original header fields elsewhere. we should document that parity.
sofia: quick mitigation options: 1) make redaction a wire-level concern (i.e., scrub right before actual socket write) so span context isn't mutated; 2) export-level fix: attach an original_request_id attribute to the span at the moment otel filter first sees the headers, store it as a separate attribute that redaction never touches; 3) change retry impl to propagate original headers via a preserved context key.
alex: I prototyped (2): in OtelContextFilter when header present do span.setAttribute("redwood.request_id.orig", headerVal) and mark it as sensitive so exporter processors redact on export if needed. tests look okay locally.
ryan: add unit test that simulates RetryFilter + RedactFilter order permutations. we should also add an exporter-level safety check that drops any attribute whose name matches sensitive_keys unless explicitly allowed.
meera: important: whichever fix we pick, ensure we don't accidentally export raw request IDs in traces for customers. add e2e test that runs sampleapp with redaction enabled and asserts no raw values in OTLP payloads.
sofia: i'll update the devex doc "hook ordering" page with a small diagram and language parity notes (java/node/python/go) + include recommended pattern: set immutable span attrs from original headers early, do wire-level redaction later.
alex: opened PR for sampleapp changes: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp/pull/7823 (WIP)
telemetry-bot: New issue opened: DEVEX-4891 "java sampleapp: request_id mutated on retry due to filter ordering" — https://issuetracker.internal/DEVEX-4891
ryan: action items: alex to finish PR + tests, sofia to update docs, meera to add e2e OTLP scrub test, i'll add exporter-level attribute whitelist and review PRs.
alex: thanks all, filing a brief RFC in the repo for exporter redaction behavior as well. :thumbsup:
